$doc: Dagr section 04, the Line of Sight flow. Manifest for AnalysisBento.tsx, which binds it to the generic ResolutionsBento adapter (components/case-studies/uscg-bard/ResolutionsBento.tsx), the same one Nuuly's AppsBento and FDT-E's GateWalkBento use. Six tiles, cut by the bento-crop skill from 4320x2700 re-exports and approved at their real rendered widths. They replace the four uncropped 2880x1800 screenshots (works-panel, works-formula, works-band, works-primary) this file carried after the scaffold pass; those four PNGs are still in public/ and are referenced by nothing.
$adapterDoc: GENERIC ADAPTER, NOT THE LEGACY ONE, AND THE REASON IS THE CAPTIONS. Resolutions01Bento reads a single caption string and splits it at the first '. ' (Resolutions01Bento.tsx splitCaption). ResolutionsBento reads caption as { lead, tail } and passes both straight through, no split. Dagr's captions carry full stops inside the tail, so the generic path is the only one that preserves the shipped strings without a round trip through a string split that could re-punctuate them. A later reader comparing this file to BARD's numbered themes should not read the choice as picking the wrong precedent.
$modeDoc: EVERY COMPOSITION ENTRY SAYS mode: 'light' AND THAT IS CORRECT, NOT A BUG TO FIX. ResolutionsBento.resolve() keys the base stem for 'light' and <name>--dark for 'dark'; it has no third value. Dagr's product is dark-only and ships one file per image, so 'light' here means 'the base stem, there is no dark twin'. FDT-E's gate-walk-manifest.json does the same thing for the same reason. Changing these to 'dark' would look right and would break the lookup.
$dimensionsDoc: width and height ARE NOT AUTHORITATIVE AND THE ADAPTER IGNORES THEM. ResolutionsBento's ManifestImage interface has no width or height, and BentoItem renders <Image fill>, so nothing here reaches the render. They are recorded for crop planning only. BARD's theme1-grid-manifest.json carries width and height that ARE load-bearing on the legacy path, so these look identical to numbers that matter. RE-READ THEM FROM DISK on any later edit rather than trusting what is written here. Every value in this pass was re-read with sips from the copied file rather than carried over from the crop spec.
$ratioDoc: ratio describes the file and is derived from the file on disk every time this manifest is written, never copied forward. In the crops staging manifest 04-03-formula read '1920:1200' after its box had been widened to 2160x1350; the value stayed numerically correct at 1.600 and was still a lie about the file. Any value that describes a file must be re-read when the file changes.
$slotDoc: BentoItem renders <Image fill> with object-fit cover, so a slot whose aspect differs from the crop silently takes the sides off, and no lint check catches it. 04-03 and 04-05 were cut at 16:10 and briefed as standard (3:4); they are wide (16:10) and cover-crop nothing. 04-07 is 12:7, which matches no slot, so it is a band: a band takes free aspect and cannot cover-crop. Note that wide's WIDEST render is 660px in the 768 to 1023 band where it goes one-up, not its 536px desktop half-container render, which is why its retina floor is 1320 and not 1072.
$orderDoc: FILE NUMBERS ARE NOT DOCUMENT ORDER. Section 04 runs 02, 04, 03, 05, 06, 07 so that the two 3:4 panel tiles pair in one row and the two 16:10 tiles pair in the next. The files are deliberately NOT renamed to match: the composition array below names tiles explicitly, so order never comes from filenames, and renaming files this manifest references would trade a cosmetic confusion for a real one.
$compositionDoc: Four rows, each aspect-consistent: [standard, standard] at 0.750, [wide, wide] at 1.600, [feature] at 1.600, then the band, which self-isolates at its document position. bento.tsx overrideRows chunks consecutive same-slot items at SLOT_COLS capacity, so each pair would form a row whether or not it is bracketed; the bracket states the intent and does not enforce it. FDT-E's composition entries repeat breakout and aspect alongside name and mode. Those copies are INERT: renderTile reads breakout and aspect from the images record that resolve() returns, never from the composition entry. Dagr states each fact once, in images, because a second copy nothing reads is a copy that goes stale silently. Do not restore the duplication as a missing field.

images.alt: The Line of Sight panel open over the map for BAR LOCK RADAR: Antenna Height reading 59.64 (default) ft, an altitude of 15,000 being typed into the MSL field below it, and an existing list headed Antenna Height: 59.64 ft (default) running from 35,000 down to 32,500 MSL.

caption.tail: Carried in from the equipment record. The analyst types the altitude and nothing else.

images.alt: The same panel with Antenna Height changed to 100.00 and a revert arrow beside the field, an empty Add altitude control, and two collapsed group headers below it: Antenna Height: 59.64 ft (default), and Antenna Height: 100.00 ft.

caption.tail: A changed height starts its own group, and the default set stays intact.

images.alt: A dialog over the parameters panel with three fields: Max Altitude 35,000 MSL, Min Altitude 33,000 MSL, and Altitude Threshold 500 ft, above CANCEL and DONE. Behind it the altitude list already holds 35,000 down to 33,000 MSL.

caption.tail: A maximum, a minimum and a threshold generate the whole band in one submit.

images.alt: A toast over the terrain reading 35,000 MSL removed, with an UNDO action and a dismiss cross. The altitude list behind it now starts at 34,500 MSL, and the remaining polygons stay drawn beside the radar's marker.

caption.tail: Removing an altitude can be undone from the toast that reports it.

images.alt: The Line of Sight panel beside a wide terrain view: five altitude entries from 35,000 down to 33,000 MSL, each with its own colour swatch, and five overlapping polygons fanning east from the radar's marker across the ridges.

caption.tail: Each polygon is the ground the radar can see from that height, cut by the terrain between.

images.alt: A row menu open on the 35,000 MSL layer with three items: Set as Mission Altitude, Resubmit Analysis, and Remove. The rest of the altitude list continues below, and that layer's polygon stays drawn on the map beside it.

caption.tail: The analyst marks the altitude he plans against. The rest stay on the map to check it against.
